title: Alien Dictionary
description: You are given words claimed to be lexicographically sorted under an unknown alphabet. Infer an ordering of all distinct letters from the list; any ordering that satisfies every adjacent pair is accepted. Return an empty string when no ordering can explain the list, including when a longer word precedes its own prefix.

examples.explain: z is ordered before o; any consistent ordering scores full marks.
examples.raw:
Input: words = ["z","o"]
Output: "zo"
Explanation: z is ordered before o; any consistent ordering scores full marks.

examples.explain: One ordering consistent with every adjacent pair.
examples.raw:
Input: words = ["hrn","hrf","er","enn","rfnn"]
Output: "hernf"
Explanation: One ordering consistent with every adjacent pair.

examples.explain: A longer word before its own prefix contradicts sorted order.
examples.raw:
Input: words = ["abc","ab"]
Output: ""
Explanation: A longer word before its own prefix contradicts sorted order.

constraints: words consist of lowercase English letters
any ordering satisfying all adjacent pairs is accepted
hints: Compare each adjacent pair only up to the first differing letter; that pair orders the two letters.
A longer word before its own prefix is impossible, so answer empty.
Topological order of the letter graph is a valid alphabet; cycles mean no answer.
solution: Turn first differing letters of adjacent words into precedence edges, then emit a topological order; a missing order means contradiction. Any valid order grades as correct.
